findings.claim: Coronation ceremonies, introduced in the tenth century, placed the king in a sacred role as God's anointed ruler.
findings.truth: Anointing of English kings is attested from 787 (Ecgfrith of Mercia). What is tenth-century is the developed English coronation order used at Edgar's crowning in 973. The sentence is loose rather than wrong at GCSE level.
findings.evidence: general knowledge of the English coronation ordines

findings.claim: The death of Queen Anne without heirs led to the Act of Union with Scotland (1707).
findings.truth: Anne died on 1 August 1714, seven years after the Union. Her death cannot have caused it. What shaped the Union was the prospect that she would die without an heir, after the death of her son in 1700 and the Scottish Act of Security of 1704.
findings.evidence: regnal dates of Queen Anne; Acts of Union 1707

findings.claim: in June 1688 ordered the Church of England to read his Declaration of Indulgence from every pulpit
findings.truth: The second Declaration of Indulgence was issued on 27 April 1688 and the Order in Council commanding it to be read in churches was made on 4 May 1688. Readings ran from 20 May.
findings.evidence: dates of the second Declaration of Indulgence and the Order in Council

findings.claim: William III and Mary II were crowned jointly in April 1689 after accepting the Bill of Rights.
findings.truth: They accepted the Declaration of Right in February 1689 and were crowned in April. Parliament enacted it as the Bill of Rights in December 1689, after the coronation.
findings.evidence: sequence of the Declaration of Right and the Bill of Rights 1689

findings.claim: directly violating the constitutional settlement of 1689's predecessor
findings.truth: Garbled and anachronistic: James II acted in 1687-88 and cannot have violated a settlement made after he was deposed. What he overrode were the penal laws Parliament had already passed.
findings.evidence: internal logic; James II deposed December 1688

findings.claim: The Second Reform Act of 1867 was 'passed by Benjamin Disraeli's Conservative government' (repeated in the glossary, a knowledge-check match pair and a flashcard).
findings.truth: Two defensible readings. Strictly the Prime Minister in 1867 was the 14th Earl of Derby; Disraeli was Chancellor and led the Bill through the Commons, becoming PM only in February 1868. But 'Disraeli's Conservative government' is the standard GCSE shorthand and correcting it ripples through four fields. Options: (a) leave the shorthand, (b) change all four to 'the Conservative government of Derby and Disraeli'.
findings.evidence: ministerial dates of Derby and Disraeli

findings.claim: DORA allowed the government to ... conscript men into the armed forces (repeated in the key fact, a flashcard and a practice mark scheme).
findings.truth: DORA (8 August 1914) did not introduce conscription. Conscription came with the Military Service Act of January 1916. Presenting it as a DORA power would cost marks in a question on state power in the First World War.
findings.evidence: Defence of the Realm Act 1914; Military Service Act 1916

findings.claim: The Emergency Powers (Defence) Act (1939) gave Churchill's wartime coalition even more sweeping powers than DORA.
findings.truth: The Act was passed on 24 August 1939 under Neville Chamberlain. Churchill did not become Prime Minister until May 1940.
findings.evidence: Emergency Powers (Defence) Act 1939; Chamberlain's ministry

findings.claim: When the Conservatives returned to power under Winston Churchill in 1951, they did not dismantle the NHS or the nationalised industries.
findings.truth: They kept the NHS and most nationalised industries but denationalised iron and steel and road haulage in 1953. The blanket claim is wrong.
findings.evidence: Iron and Steel Act 1953; Transport Act 1953

findings.claim: creating the first peacetime coalition government in Britain since 1945 (repeated in the key fact and the conclusion).
findings.truth: The coalition that ended in 1945 was the wartime coalition, so 'peacetime coalition since 1945' does not work. 2010 was the first coalition government of any kind since the Second World War; the last peacetime one was the National Government of the 1930s.
findings.evidence: Churchill war ministry 1940-45; National Government 1931-40

summary: All ten lessons carried another board's practice labels: the OCR thematic paper is 50 marks in one hour with Describe 4, Explain 8, a 14-mark second-order concept question and a 24-mark change-and-continuity essay, and it carries no SPaG marks (the spec puts the two 5-mark SPaG allocations on paper 1 question 4 and paper 3 question 2). Beyond the labels, the substantive errors were eight fabricated examiner claims, conscription wrongly given as a DORA power, Queen Anne's 1714 death given as the cause of the 1707 Union, Emily Davison killed on the day of the Derby, Elizabeth I's ten parliaments counted as thirteen, and an unverified Thatcher self-quotation.
